title: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Designates the Troubadour as a Landmark Venue, With Ceremony to Precede Gram Parsons Tribute Concert (EXCLUSIVE)
description: The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame is designating the legendary Troubadour as a Landmark in music history, with a ceremony to make it official set to tak
body:
The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame is designating the legendary Troubadour as a Landmark in music history, with a ceremony to make it official set to take place Wednesday afternoon at the West Hollywood nightclub, among the first of several days of events in L.A. leading up to Saturday night’s annual Hall of Fame induction concert.

	The Landmark dedication will take place Wednesday at 3 p.m., a few hours before the venue hosts a sold out tribute show in honor of the late Gram Parsons, who will become a Hall of Fame inductee Saturday.
	

	an official Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Landmark designation, recognizing the venue’s extraordinary contributions to music history. For decades, the iconic venue has served as a launching pad for emerging artists and helped shape the sound of Southern California music. The dedication will take place ahead of the evening’s sold-out tribute to 2026 Inductee Gram Parsons

	“Los Angeles has played an important role in shaping popular music since the ’60s, and the Troubadour is one of the places where that history really came to life,” John Sykes, chairman of the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame since 2020, tells Variety. “Elton John is just one of the artists who got their first break here. When you look at the other landmarks the Hall has recognized, whether it’s the Ryman Auditorium, the Bottom Line, the Surf Ballroom or King Records, each has played a vital role in the evolution of music. The Troubadour has that same kind of significance, shining a light on the role independent clubs continue to play in live music. They’re places where artists can take chances, find their audience and develop their sound before the rest of the world catches on.”
	

	The first event put on by the Hall of Fame this week will come Tuesday night, when the Morrison Gallery (also located in West Hollywood, inside the Sunset Marquis hotel) will host the opening of an exhibition titled “Snapshot: The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame In Focus,” featuring seen and previously unseen photographs of inductees, including the incoming class of 2026.

	Wednesday the action moves just slightly southwest, with the dedication event at the Troubadour in the afternoon and the Gram Parsons salute at the venerable club in the evening. That show, co-presented by the Parsons Estate, which sold out instantaneously, will feature Emmylou Harris, Elvis Costello, the Black Crowes, Jesse Welles, Margo Price, Grace Potter and many other Parsons acolytes.

	On Friday, the Grammy Museum will host a conversation with Peter Hook of Joy Division and New Order, the overlapping bands who will be jointly inducted into the Hall Saturday night. The conversation with Hook at the 200-seat Clive Davis Theater will be moderated by the Rock Hall’s VP of education, Jason Hanley. And then Saturday is the induction ceremony at the Peacock Theater, for which some tickets are still on sale. 

	The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame ceremonies shift between L.A., New York and the Hall’s home city, Cleveland. Sykes explains why they elongated the days leading up to this year’s SoCal ceremony into something approaching a Hall of Fame Week.

	“The first decision I made when taking over the role as chairman of the Hall of Fame was to make a dedicated commitment to our presence in Los Angeles,” he says. “Since the inaugural Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony in 1986, Los Angeles had hosted just two ceremonies prior to 2020. Since then, we have brought the ceremony to LA three additional times, bringing the total to five. With Los Angeles now established as a regular part of the rotation alongside New York and Cleveland, we can expect to be here at least every other year, if not more frequently.

	“With our increased presence in the West, we see an opportunity to make the ceremony the cornerstone of a week-long celebration,” Sykes continues. “There’s an incredible music history here, an incredible creative community, and so many stories worth celebrating. The Gram Parsons tribute at the Troubadour is a great example of that. It’s a chance to recognize an artist in a setting that has a real connection to his story, and to bring together artists from different generations to celebrate his influence.”
	

	Of the Parsons show specifically, the Hall of Fame chairman says, “I think it’s a special celebration of the music history of Los Angeles. Gram Parsons was an incredibly influential artist who helped change the direction of American music. He brought country, rock, soul and other influences together, especially in this town, in a way that hadn’t really been done before, and you can hear his influence in generations of artists who followed him. The Troubadour is the perfect venue to celebrate Parson’s influence. You have artists like Emmylou Harris, who shared such an important musical partnership with Gram, alongside Elvis Costello, the Black Crowes, Margo Price and a new generation of artists who continue to carry that influence forward.”

	The class of 2026, including those who were voted in and those selected for special honors by the board, includes Phil Collins, Billy Idol, Iron Maiden, Joy Division/New Order, Oasis, Sade, Luther Vandross and Wu-Tang Clan in the Performer category; Celia Cruz, Fela Kuti, Queen Latifah, MC Lyte and Parsons for Early Influence; Linda Creed, Arif Mardin, Jimmy Miller and Rick Rubin for Musical Excellence; and Ed Sullivan for the Ahmet Ertegun Award.

	This year’s induction ceremony is not being livestreamed, as it has been in other recent years, so it will remain a you-had-to-be-there experience until a special airs on ABC in just under a month, on Dec. 8.

	There will, however, be a red carpet livestream, beginning Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET/4:30 p.m. PT, co-hosted by Allison Hagendorf and Maria Ferrer, streaming live on the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame’s official YouTube channel.

	The special being filmed at the induction ceremony, besides premiering on Disney Dec. 8, will be available the following day on Disney+ and Hulu.

schema.headline: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Designates the Troubadour as a Landmark Venue, With Ceremony to Precede Gram Parsons Tribute Concert (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Kiah Roache-Turner Reunites With ‘Furiosa’ Star Alyla Browne on ‘Horrifically Creepy’ Road Movie Horror ‘Don’t Look’: ‘There Are Scenes That Are Going to Traumatize People’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Australian genre filmmaker Kiah Roache-Turner (“Sting,” “Beast of War”) is set to direct upcoming horror “Don’t Look,” reuniting him with fast-risi
body:
Australian genre filmmaker Kiah Roache-Turner (“Sting,” “Beast of War”) is set to direct upcoming horror “Don’t Look,” reuniting him with fast-rising star (and fellow antipodean) Alyla Browne (“Furiosa”). 

	The film — which was previously entitled “From Below” and was to be the directorial debut of writer Sean Loch — is being sold by Cornerstone at the American Film Market. Roache-Turner — currently in post on WWI action-horror movie “Lady Death” — has taken over directing duties due to scheduling issues.
	

	“Don’t Look” is described as a “fresh take” on the road movie horror, where the “true source of fear remains elusive and unseen.” Speaking to Variety, Roache-Turner simply said it was “scary as all hell” with scenes are “going to traumatise people very deeply.”

	Set against the backdrop of the Australian outback, the film follows 15-year-old Riley (Browne), travelling across the outback with her father when they come across two seemingly abandoned cars at an isolated desert crossing. When an invisible force drags her father away Riley finds herself in a life-or-death struggle against a terrifying creature that is only visible to its next victim.

	Alongside Browne — who starred in Roache-Turner’s spider horror “Sting” and whose credits also include “Sonic the Hedgehog 3” and “Nine Perfect Strangers” — will appear alongside George Pullar (“Evil Dead Burn”), Masha Basman (“Bay of Fires”) and Stephen Peacocke (“Me Before You”). 

	“Don’t Look” was developed with filmmaker Joel Anderson (“Late Night with the Devil,” “Lake Mungo”).  Loch’s original screenplay was featured on The Black List, trending under “Top Horror Scripts” for six weeks. Producers include Blake Northfield (“Lady Death,” “Beast of War”) and Sam Price (“Rear View Mirror,” “Leech”) 
	

	Speaking to Variety, Roache-Turner discusses boarding the project and working once more with Browne. 
	
		What was it about ‘Dont Look’ that drew you in?	

	Quite simply that it was one of the best scripts I’ve ever read. I was intrigued at first by the premise and the idea of a single-location, desert-set creature feature. When Sean approached me with the idea of directing it my tongue nearly got whiplash I said yes so fast.
	
		‘Don’t Look’ is described as a ‘fresh take’ on the road movie horror. Can you explain a little more about this?	

	I’m a big fan of the road movie horror genre – I can’t get enough of films like “Wolf Creek, “Texas Chainsaw Massacre,” “The Hitcher” and “Jeepers Creepers.” But what I found refreshing about “Don’t Look” was the layered and fertile character work; how the emotional setups were handled with such precision and how they all paid off so cleverly in the final act. It also helps that the central creature feels truly original, terrifying and disturbing in a way that I’ve never seen portrayed in a monster movie before.
	
		You’re reuniting with Alyla Brown after Sting. How excited are you about that? Have you been keeping in touch with her since then (and following her impressive career)?	

	I am extremely excited to be working with Alyla again! We’ve certainly kept in touch. Every time I see her on a new movie poster it makes me happy. She’s going to be a massive star one day so I want to make as many films with her as I can before she gets too famous and Spielberg snaps her up. She was 12 when we started filming “Sting” and even back then she was one of the most naturally talented and professional actors I’ve ever worked with. She turned 17 halfway through the filming of our last collaboration [a family film about endurance riding called “Chiquita”). But her character in “Don’t Look” is a lot darker and deeper than anything we’ve done before. 
	
		So far you’ve battled zombies, giant spiders, sharks, and whatever the monsters in “Lady Death” are. What sort of horrors are we up against in “Don’t Look”	

	Well, I don’t want to give the game away but we’re up against a monster that I’ve never really seen before onscreen. It’s such weird creature and so beautifully and horrifically creepy that I’ve decided to change my entire visual style just to accommodate Sean’s insanely original narrative. All I can say at this stage is that it’s as scary as all hell and there are scenes in this movie that are going to traumatise people very deeply. Of course, those are the scenes I’m most looking forward to directing!

title: DC Studios’ New Boss Jeremy Latcham Has a ‘Guiding Light’ for Superhero Movies: Would My Grandma Like It? ‘You Have to Make Them for Everybody’
description: Jeremy Latcham is the new president and chief creative officer of DC Studios, taking over duties after James Gunn and Peter Safran’s four-year stin
body:
Jeremy Latcham is the new president and chief creative officer of DC Studios, taking over duties after James Gunn and Peter Safran’s four-year stint. So what does that mean for the future of the DC Universe? It’s a question comic book movie fans are now asking on social media, and one that has led them to recent interviews with Latcham that suggest the post-Gunn and Safran era of DC movies and TV shows will align more with four-quadrant crowdpleasers than with edgier fare.
	

	“When we were making the first Marvel movies I would always be like, ‘I don’t know if my grandma would like that.’ That became a guiding light… it became the stand-in for ‘is this going to work for regular people outside the bubble of Hollywood?’ Latcham said over the summer while talking to Christian Broadcasting News (via GamesRadar) about his previous comic book movie philosophy.

	Latcham notably joined Marvel Studios in 2004 and rose to senior VP of production and development, working closely with president Kevin Feige to launch the Marvel Cinematic Universe as an associate producer on “Iron Man.” He went to co-produce “Iron Man 2” and executive produce “The Avengers,” “Guardians of the Galaxy,” “Avengers: Age of Ultron” and “Spider-Man: Homecoming.”

	“In the old Marvel days, there’s this great story about my Meemaw and Peepaw because they became, like, a joke in the editing room – that we were making the movie for my grandparents in Oklahoma,” Latcham previously said in a separate interview with GamesRadar+. “If they weren’t gonna understand it, [it was] never going to work for anybody… I think that’s kind of the fun of these movies, of adapting material – finding a way to make it for everybody. You have to be true to the fans, but you have to make it ultimately for everybody.”
	

	Latcham left Marvel in 2017 to found Latcham Pictures, which produced movies such as “Bad Times at the El Royale” and “Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves.” 

	In his statement on becoming the new boss of DC Studios, Latcham said: “DC’s pantheon of characters is among the most iconic in American popular culture. I’ve had the privilege to help bring some of the most celebrated superhero stories to life on the big screen, and I’m excited and honored for the opportunity to now lead DC Studios into its next era. The chance to steward the incredible cast of DC characters to the screen in a way that excites lifelong fans while introducing their timeless stories to the next generation is a massive responsibility that I do not take lightly.”

schema.headline: DC Studios’ New Boss Jeremy Latcham Has a ‘Guiding Light’ for Superhero Movies: Would My Grandma Like It? ‘You Have to Make Them for Everybody’

body:
Nurse John is scrubbing up for a 2027 tour.

	The Los Angeles-based stand-up comedian and viral social media creator will hit the road in January for the “Against Medical Advice: Readmitted Tour,” the second leg of a run that sold more than 75,000 tickets.

	This leg kicks off in Arizona and sees John hitting Vancouver, Kentucky, New York, Las Vegas and more North American cities before he wraps up in Alaska in May.


	Pre-sales begin to roll out on Wednesday, Nov. 11 at 10 a.m. local time. A general on-sale begins on Friday, Nov. 13 at 10 a.m. local time.
	

	“I never imagined that a Filipino kid with big dreams would one day stand on the iconic stage of Radio City Music Hall,” John said in a statement. “I’m filled with so much gratitude for how far I’ve come and for everyone who believed in me. Everything I do comes from a place of love and the hope that my journey reminds someone out there that no dream is too big, no matter where you come from.”

title: David Walliams Speaks Out on Allegations: ‘I Am Not a Sexual Predator’
description: Comedian, author and former “Britain’s Got Talent” judge David Walliams has denied that he is a sexual predator, following publication of allegatio
body:
Comedian, author and former “Britain’s Got Talent” judge David Walliams has denied that he is a sexual predator, following publication of allegations in the Guardian.

	According to a statement published by the BBC, Walliams said, “Looking back, I realize that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with.

	“I realize I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret.
	

	“And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did.”

	He added: “I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.”

	The Guardian on Tuesday alleged that Walliams “groomed fans he met when they were as young as 15 and harassed women in the workplace over a number of years.” He denies the allegations.

	Among the allegations, which were made during a joint investigation by the Guardian and ITN, is that Walliams was “predatory” and “pushy,” repeatedly contacting young women either via social media or modelling agencies, inviting them to his home or his dressing room at “Britain’s Got Talent.” One woman, who became friendly with the comedian after he contacted her, said he would “constantly pester her for sex.”

	The report also alleged that Walliams would message “young female runners” who worked on his productions as well as staff at his publisher, HarperCollins.
	

	Walliams has denied any wrongdoing, including any allegations of sexual harassment or inappropriate behavior.

	Earlier this month, it was revealed that an anonymous celebrity had applied for a court injunction at the London High Court to try to prevent ITN and the Guardian from publishing a story about him containing allegations that he abused his power to engage in “inappropriate sexual activities with a large number of girls and young women,” according to BBC News.

	Walliams was not granted the injunction, meaning that these allegations may now be made public by the news organizations. He told the court that if the injunction was not granted and the stories were published, it was “highly likely” he would attempt to commit suicide. His lawyer told the court he had already attempted to do so twice before.

schema.headline: David Walliams Speaks Out on Allegations: ‘I Am Not a Sexual Predator’

title: ‘Overcompensating’ Season 2 Release Date: Benito Skinner Returns for a Steamy Spring Semester (TV News Roundup)
description:
“Overcompensating” is back for the spring semester with Season 2 hitting Prime Video on Feb. 17.

	Created, written and executive produced by Benit
body:
“Overcompensating” is back for the spring semester with Season 2 hitting Prime Video on Feb. 17.

	Created, written and executive produced by Benito Skinner, the 2010’s college dramedy follows Skinner playing himself as a closeted former football player and homecoming king, navigating college and his identity with his best friend Carmen (Wally Baram), and the guidance of his older sister (Mary Beth Barone).


	Per the logline, “Season 2 finds Benny and his friends in their second semester, juggling new lovers, cringey encounters, sexual awakenings, and riskiest of all: collegiate sports. Deeply funny and personal, the show explores the lengths to which we all overcompensate while on the path to finding out who we really are.”
	

	Skinner, Baram and Barone are joined by returning cast members Adam DiMarco, Rish Shah, Holmes, Owen Thiele, Kyle MacLachlan, Connie Britton, Lukas Gage and Nell Verlaque.

	The series is produced by A24, Strong Baby and Amazon MGM Studios. Scott King also serves as showrunner and executive producer. Additional executive producers include A24; Jonah Hill, Matt Dines and Ali Goodwin for Strong Baby; and returning executive producer Charli XCX.

	See below for more first-look photos.




	

	






	

	





	

	





	

	





	

	


	
		DEVELOPMENT/PRODUCTION	

	National Geographic has greenlit “The Real Frozen,” a natural history series exploring the real-world landscapes and animals that inspired Disney’s “Frozen.”

	Kristen Bell, Idina Menzel, Josh Gad and Jonathan Groff will reprise their characters to guide viewers through arctic landscapes across Iceland, Finland, Norway and Sweden. Designed as though the animated characters were exploring the real world, the docuseries follows the lives of animals whose demanding journey to survive the winter inspired the “emotional heart” of the Disney film.

	In collaboration with Walt Disney Animation Studios, “The Real Frozen” will premiere on National Geographic and stream on Disney+ and Hulu. The docuseries is produced by Silverback Films for National Geographic. For Silverback Films, Jeff Wilson directs the series, and Elisabeth Oakham and Katie Parsons serve as director and producers on all episodes. For National Geographic, Janet H. Vissering is executive producer, and Tom McDonald is executive vice president of content.
	
	
		DATES	

	Fox Entertainment’s docuseries “The Well” is now streaming on Hulu, investigating more than 200 unsolved murders in California’s San Joaquin County, including those linked to the Speed Freak Killers.

	Years after the killers’ were incacerated, a new cold case unit led by Lieutenant Linda Jimenez is reopened. Determined to find the remains of victims who are still missing, Jimenez seeks help from convicted serial killer Wesley Shermantine, whose hand-drawn maps may hold the answers she’s looking for.

	All six episodes are available to stream on Hulu and Hulu on Disney+ for bundle subscribers in the U.S.. “The Well” is produced by Fox Entertainment Studios, Mountain Top Pictures, Haven Entertainment and Fairvale Entertainment. Rachel Witte, Michael Bott, Toby Louie, Nicolas Levene, Kevin Mann and Mark Ankner serve as executive producers, with Michael Horn as as co-executive producer.

title: Adobe Is Adding AI Agent Features Across Its Product Lines, but Execs Emphasize Creators Have Choice of How They Use AI
description: Adobe is embracing AI in an effort to make its suite of creative tools more powerful and efficient than ever. But the company also recognizes that
body:
Adobe is embracing AI in an effort to make its suite of creative tools more powerful and efficient than ever. But the company also recognizes that not all of its customers want to use AI in their work. 

	In the kickoff keynote session for Adobe MAX 2026 creativity conference, Adobe’s incoming CEO Anil Chakravarthy announced that the company is expanding the Adobe Creative Agent across Creative Cloud and Adobe Firefly — so they can hand off complex, multistep tasks to an AI assistant.
	

	The challenge for creative pros, Chakravarthy said in his keynote remarks, is “at a time when there’s such a flood of creative output, how do you stand out?” Some Adobe users don’t want “anything to do with AI” but “we’ve heard from many others who are interested — even excited — in it.”

	Adobe is in the midst of a CEO changeover: Chakravarthy, president of Adobe’s Customer Experience Orchestration business and worldwide field operations, is set to become the company’s next president and CEO effective Dec. 1. Shantanu Narayen, after nearly 20 years as CEO, will move into a role as Adobe’s executive chair.

	The company’s goal is to deliver tools that fuel creativity “without compromising your craft, your control or your rights,” Narayen told attendees. With AI, a key part of its approach is to give users the option to use AI-powered features or not, he said.

	At MAX, Adobe is previewing local Model Context Protocol integrations for Creative Cloud tools that will let users direct third-party agents they already use to make changes in their native project files in Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and After Effects.
	

	Adobe said it has expanded partnerships with Google and Microsoft and is building on collaborations with Anthropic and OpenAI. With Google, Adobe is putting its creative and productivity tools in more Google products and experiences, adding Google’s latest frontier AI models to Adobe’s tools and exploring new AI-powered editing capabilities for Photoshop with Google DeepMind. With Microsoft, Adobe is delivering optimized versions of Photoshop, Premiere, After Effects and Substance 3D Painter (beta) for high-performance Arm-based Windows PCs, and access to Adobe Express’ quick and easy creation tools in Microsoft Photos on Windows.

	The company announced that Adobe Firefly, its AI creative studio, is bringing a choice of top industry AI models — including from such partners as ByteDance, Google, Kling, OpenAI and ElevenLabs — and the Adobe Creative Agent together in one place.

	For Firefly, the company plans to add “always-on agents” for creative workflows that can take on recurring tasks (for example, organizing incoming assets and checking quality to preparing content for different channels) — and continue working in the background even when creators step away.

	Adobe announced Firefly Video, a single workflow for assembling videos ranging from social content to short films, and Firefly Design (beta), a new design editing space that brings together tools for illustration, image editing, animation, 3D and print on a single canvas. In addition, there’s Firefly Image, a set of new editing tools that give creators the control to change just one part of an image and keep everything else as it was with Edit Object, along with Relight and Retouch that pair prompt-based edits with manual precision.

	In addition, Adobe announced Firefly Builder (available in private beta), a new tool that helps creators transform ideas into interactive prototypes, like a website, presentation or app, using natural language commands.

	In Adobe GenStudio, its toolset for marketers, a new conversational AI interface allows users to direct campaign planning, creation and activation while Coworker coordinates AI agents and workflows. The company said Adobe Brand Intelligence, an agent designed to enforce brand standards, is expanding its capabilities with Intelligent Reflow, letting teams automatically adapt designs to new sizes and layouts (a feature also coming to Photoshop Illustrator and InDesign).
	

	The theme of Adobe MAX 2026, being held Nov. 10-12 in Miami Beach, is “Dream Big. Create Bigger.” The company recently announced has more than 1 billion active monthly users worldwide for its products.

	On Monday, Adobe announced a multiyear strategic partnership with Disney, becoming an “official AI innovation partner.” Under that agreement, Adobe technology will support “concept exploration” in Disney’s innovation labs as well as parks and cruise development pipelines using custom AI models and tools.

	RELATED: Disney Taps Adobe as ‘Official AI Innovation Partner’ Under Multiyear Pact

title: Fantastic Fest Award Winner ‘Bloody Tennis,’ Starring Sandra Guldberg Kampp and Helena Zengel, Sells to Further Territories (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Fantastic Fest award winner “Bloody Tennis,” starring Sandra Guldberg Kampp and Golden Globe nominee Helena Zengel, has sold to several further ter
body:
Fantastic Fest award winner “Bloody Tennis,” starring Sandra Guldberg Kampp and Golden Globe nominee Helena Zengel, has sold to several further territories, ahead of its market premiere this week at the American Film Market in Los Angeles.

	Nikias Chryssos‘ English-language horror film has been acquired in the U.K. and Ireland by Blue Finch, in Turkey by Bir Film and in Ukraine by Svoe Kino.


	The new deals join previously announced sales to Shudder (U.S.), Umbrella Entertainment (Australia), BestFilm.eu (Baltics), Plaion Pictures (Italy), Extreme Film (Japan), 9th Plan (Poland), Gulf Film (Middle East) and Njutafilms (Scandinavia). The German distributor is Port au Prince.
	

	The Playmaker Munich is handling international sales.

	The film had its world premiere at Locarno Film Festival on Aug. 7 and went on to win best director among horror features at Fantastic Fest  in Austin and the Méliès d’Argent in the feature film category at Slash Filmfestival. Other festivals screenings included Sitges, Thessaloniki and Tallinn Black Nights.

	“Bloody Tennis” stars Guldberg Kampp (“Foundation”), Zengel (“News of the World,” “The Legend of Ochi”), Tracy Gotoas (“Safe House”), Lucie Zhang (“Paris, 13th District”), Lily Taïeb (“The French Dispatch,” “Bergman Island”), Elina Löwensohn (“Schindler’s List”), Zlatko Burić (“Triangle of Sadness”), Juliana Vieira Guerra and Vincent Romeo.

	It has an original score from Jim Williams (“Titane,” “Raw” and “Possessor”). Cinematography is by Constantin Campean.

	The film centers on Sophie (Guldberg Kampp) who is admitted to an elite tennis academy hidden deep in Southern Europe. There she must contend not only with the fierce brutality of her teammates but with the school’s increasingly sinister undercurrents, where competitive sports are taken to their extreme and only the hungriest survive.
	

	The film “takes the world of elite sports to disturbing new heights, filled with brutal ambition, blood-sucking leeches and hard-hitting serves,” according to a statement from The Playmaker Munich. 

	The film is produced by Jonas Katzenstein and Maximilian Leo (“The Weight,” “The Assessment,” “Mother Mary”) of Augenschein Filmproduktion in co-production with Port au Prince Film & Kultur Produktion and ZDF – Das Kleine Fernsehspiel.

	Chryssos’ first feature film “Der Bunker” premiered at the Berlin Film Festival, and won the Next Wave Award for best feature at Fantastic Fest in Austin. His second feature film, “A Pure Place,” was developed at the Résidence of Cannes Film Festival and premiered at the Munich Film Festival, where it won the award for best director.

schema.headline: Fantastic Fest Award Winner ‘Bloody Tennis,’ Starring Sandra Guldberg Kampp and Helena Zengel, Sells to Further Territories (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Heated Rivalry’ Final Episodes to Release in 4DX at Regal Theaters
description: If just watching “Heated Rivalry” wasn’t steamy enough, fans can now feel the heat — literally — seeing the fifth and sixth episodes of the queer h
body:
If just watching “Heated Rivalry” wasn’t steamy enough, fans can now feel the heat — literally — seeing the fifth and sixth episodes of the queer hockey series in 4DX at Regal Theaters nationwide starting Nov. 16.

	“Fans made it loud and clear that they wanted more ‘Heated Rivalry’ on the big screen, so we’re turning up the heat,” Brooks LeBoeuf, senior vice president of U.S. content at Regal, said in a statement. “Episodes five and six bring years of tension between Shane and Ilya to a boiling point, and 4DX takes it all to another level. Together with CJ 4DPLEX, we’re giving fans a chance to feel every hit on the ice, every stolen embrace and every pulse-pounding moment in between. You may know these episodes by heart, but you’ve never experienced them like this.”
	

	The 4DX screenings will feature motion-enabled seating and synchronized atmospheric effects, according to Regal.

	Based on Rachel Reid’s bestselling “Game Changers” book series, adapted by Jacob Tierney, “Heated Rivalry” follows the illicit and decades-spanning relationship between two rival hockey stars, Shane Hollander (Hudson Williams) and Ilya Rozanov (Connor Storrie). The tender romance quickly became a global phenomenon and is currently in production for its second season.

	While fans wait, they can attend special 4DX paired screening of episodes “I’ll Believe in Anything” and “The Cottage” at all 59 Regal 4DX auditoriums across 59 theaters nationwide, as well as other participating locations.

	If the show alone provides enough sensation, audiences can revisit the series in standard format across three paired screenings: Episodes 1 and 2 (“Rookies” and “Olympians”), Episodes 3 and 4 (“Hunter” and “Rose”), and Episodes 5 and 6 (“I’ll Believe in Anything” and “The Cottage”). Tickets for each pairing cost $9.99.

title: ‘Later Daters’ Gets Celebrity-Filled Season 2: Christie Brinkley, Margaret Cho, Vivica A. Fox and More Seek Love in Netflix Series (EXCLUSIVE)

	The Netflix reality series, executive produc
body:
“The Later Daters” is back with Season 2, and this time it’s celebrities seeking love later in life.

	The Netflix reality series, executive produced by Michelle Obama, has been renewed for another season, which premieres on Dec. 30 on the streamer. The show will follow five celebs — Christie Brinkley, Margaret Cho, Vivica A. Fox, Caroline Rhea and Pebe Sebert (with daughter Kesha by her side) — as they open their hearts to a whole new dating world, guided by Harvard-trained behavioral scientist and relationship coach Logan Ury.
	

	“Whether navigating the highs and heartbreaks of modern romance for the first time in years or getting a second chance at love, these women prove that finding a real connection has no expiration date,” per the logline.

	The first season of “The Later Daters” premiered on Netflix in November 2024 and followed six older singles as they embarked on blind dates with potential romantic partners. Each person would check in with Ury, who helped them navigate the unfamiliar world of modern dating, as well as their adult children and close friends, who provided sage advice. 

	“The Later Daters” hails from the Obamas’ production company Higher Ground and Boardwalk Pictures. Alongside Michelle Obama, the executive producers are Ethan Lewis, Andrew Fried, Jonathan Hausfater, Dane Lillegard, Sarina Roma, Ailee O’Neill, J.C. Begley and Cian O’Clery.

	The unscripted series is one of many projects from Higher Ground to come out this year. This past summer, the company produced Larry David’s HBO sketch comedy series “Life, Larry and the Pursuit of Unhappiness,” which even starred Barack Obama in a cameo.

title: Halle Berry's Ex Olivier Martinez Wants More Child Support for Son Maceo
description:
Halle Berry's Ex Olivier Martinez
                          I Want More of Her Money!!!
body:
Halle Berry's Ex Olivier Martinez
                          I Want More of Her Money!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 10, 2026
                            7:48 AM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Halle Berry hasn't been able to see her son Maceo much in the last month and a half, and her ex-husband, Olivier Martinez, wants more dough because it's costing him more to care for the boy the lion's share of the time.
      
    
            Remember, before the incident between Halle and her 13-year-old son that went down September 28th, she and Olivier had 50/50 joint custody. Olivier beelined it for court to get a TRO, claiming Halle put Maceo in a headlock. The judge issued the TRO and said for the time being, Halle would only get occasional visits with her son, which amount to 18%, not 50%.
      
    
            Now Olivier is saying as long as that order remains in place, it's costing him more every month because he has Maceo 82% of the time. So he's asking the judge to up the ante on child support.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Olivier says Halle currently pays him $8,000 a month in child support, plus 4.3% of any annual income she makes over $2 million ... but he wants that amount recalculated to reflect their new parenting arrangement.
      
    
            And he's opening up his own finances in the process ... revealing he earns an average of just $776 a month in acting residuals, while listing more than $17,500 in monthly expenses and proposed spending needs.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Olivier hasn't specified how much more he wants ... saying he's still waiting on Halle's financial records before submitting his proposed child support calculations.
      
    
            The exes aren't done fighting over custody, either ... with a judge setting another hearing for December 17 while leaving the current custody orders in place.

title: Late 'Looney Tunes' Voice Actor Eric Bauza Leaves Behind 7-Figure Estate
description:
'Looney Tunes' Actor Eric Bauza
                          Leaves Behind 7-Figure Estate For Son, Famil
body:
'Looney Tunes' Actor Eric Bauza
                          Leaves Behind 7-Figure Estate For Son, Family
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 10, 2026
                            6:50 AM PST
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  November 10, 2026
                                7:54 AM PST
                                    
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            'Looney Tunes' voice actor Eric Bauza left behind a hefty sum for his son and family members, TMZ has learned. 
      
    
            Eric’s brother, Edgar Alan Bauza, filed court docs seeking to serve as executor of the estate of the actor who voiced Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Tweety, and Porky Pig.
      
    
            Per the petition, Eric left behind a will naming Edgar as executor of the estate, and the docs show the estate has an estimated $700k in personal property, and another $848k in equity from real property, for a grand total of more than $1.5 million.  It's unclear whether there are any separate private trusts with additional assets.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Eric died on October 25, 2026, at the age of 46. His beneficiaries include his son Ryker, his son’s mother, Jessica, his father, Egardo, his mom, Elvria, and his niece, Kyra. 
      
    
            Following his death, Eric’s friend launched a GoFundMe for Jessica … which has raised over $51k with a goal of $75k … to pay for “ongoing household bills, everyday living expenses, travel expenses to Toronto to see Eric and Jessica's families, and any myriad of unforeseen financial challenges that may present themselves.”
      

            As we previously told you ... Eric passed away last month at the age of 46.
      
    
            The Los Angeles Medical Examiner ruled Eric’s cause of death was determined to be hypertensive cardiovascular disease … with other factors including sleep apnea and obesity. His manner of death was natural.
      
    
            Eric was an icon in the animation world ... lending his voice to a whole lineup of "Looney Tunes" favorites, including Porky Pig, Tweety Bird, Elmer Fudd, Marvin the Martian, and Road Runner.
      
    
            The animation superstar garnered more than 400 acting credits throughout his career and won three Children's & Family Emmy Awards for his voice work.

            Donald Trump calling into C-SPAN is, apparently, the funniest thing ever ... or, at least it was to a mystery woman who upstaged the president's rare appearance on the channel.
      
    
            POTUS placed a call into C-SPAN Monday night -- a seemingly impromptu dial-in to Mimi Geerges' "Washington Journal Primetime" -- and immediately a woman, not seen in the TV studio, was absolutely in stitches.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Check out the clip ... Mimi thanks the prez for coming on -- and, just as he starts speaking, a woman bursts out laughing.
      

            Neither Trump nor Mimi mention the laughter ... instead moving into the interview where the pair discussed immigration, Iran, and the House of Representatives looking to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth.
      
    
            It's unclear if the woman -- who did not sound like First Lady Melania Trump -- was with the president or somewhere at C-SPAN. We also don't know if Mimi or DJT even heard the cackling.
      
    
            As you know ... President Trump's been on a media blitz in recent days -- including an appearance on "60 Minutes" -- following the devastating losses handed to Republicans in this year's midterm election.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            He also made headlines after suggesting UFC CEO Dana White could be the new White House press secretary ... though White ultimately turned down the job.
      
    
            The administration's current political situation is no laughing matter ... though, clearly, it's giving someone the giggles!

title: Ole Miss Racist Video: Student Apologizes, Claims She Didn't Know Who Lived There
description:
Ole Miss Monkey Video
                          Student Apologizes For Shocking Clip ...
body:
Ole Miss Monkey Video
                          Student Apologizes For Shocking Clip ...
                          'Actions Were Insensitive, Inappropriate'
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 10, 2026
                            7:47 AM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            One of the University of Mississippi students caught in the shocking video making monkey noises at the door of several Black students is apologizing profusely ... and insisting it was an honest mistake
      
    
            Alaina Kunes -- an 18-year-old freshman at Ole Miss -- released a statement on Tuesday ... starting by apologizing to both the women who she offended and the university community.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            She says, "Before the incident on November 6, I never met the women involved and was unaware of their race, however, I recognize my actions were insensitive, inappropriate, and deeply harmful."
      

            Alaina insists she would never intentionally make noises or gestures like she did in the video toward a person of color ... and she says she's personally apologized to them for her actions.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            She notes she can never understand the pain she's caused them ... and she says the women she's hurt "deserve to feel seen and understood" -- while adding it's not a reflection of who she's trying to become.   
      
    
            Alaina goes on to say she and her family have received death threats and harassment in the days since the video was released ... and she thanks the authorities for ensuring their safety. She says she plans to fully cooperate with the university's investigation and asks for privacy at this time.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As we reported ... video of the incident went viral -- showing two women making the noises and gestures while a third walked behind the other two and simply glanced at the door.
      
    
            Our sources say this was supposed to be harmless, silly fun ... claiming the girls were making animal noises at several different doors as they walked by.
      
    
            The American Civil Liberties Union became involved after the incident ... noting it was looking into several complaints.
